documents.unit: AI at Lehigh (Provost / Library & Technology Services)
documents.title: Policies and Best Practices
documents.summary: Lehigh's AI policies-and-practices page sets no course-level AI rule. It reminds the community of existing data-classification and acceptable-use rules, tells students to follow instructors' course rules and the Student Code of Conduct, and gives best practices on checking output, citing AI, opting out of training and using approved tools.
documents.stance_why: The page never says AI is allowed or banned in coursework: students 'are expected to follow course-specific rules set by their instructors', and instructors are only 'advised to give students clear guidance', so the decision is handed to instructors.

units.why: Frames the page as reminders of existing policy so exploration stays 'within the bounds of policy and good practice'; this is a purpose statement for the whole page, so framework P56.
units.anchor: foster responsible exploration within the bounds of policy and good practice
units.frag_start: In order to foster responsible exploration

units.why: Says 'we will treat that data ethically and in accordance with legal requirements', a statement of the institution's duty toward protected data, so P50 (protect personal data).
units.anchor: we will treat that data ethically and in accordance with legal requirements

units.why: Bans any AI tool on Class I Critical data ('no AI tool may be used'), a data-protection rule, hence P50 and must-not.
units.anchor: no AI tool may be used with Class I Critical data

units.why: Class II Restricted data 'is permitted only with tools explicitly approved', a narrow permission tied to vetted tools, so P50 and may with restrict stance.
units.anchor: is permitted only with tools explicitly approved for that classification
units.frag_start: Use of AI tools with Class II

units.why: Tells users to 'consult the Data Classification Matrix' before submitting institutional data to confirm the tool is approved; a vetted-tool and data rule (P50).
units.anchor: Before submitting any institutional data, consult the Data Classification Matrix
units.frag_end: is approved for your data's classification

units.why: Asks users with a use case involving sensitive data to 'submit an ITS consultation request'; this is a data-safety procedure so P50 rather than P63 (faculty learning).
units.anchor: submit an ITS consultation request so we can advise you
units.frag_start: If you have a use case
units.policy: Users with a Generative AI use case that involves such data submit an ITS consultation request so ITS can advise them.

units.why: Requires anyone aware of a breach 'to report the incident' to Information Security; it is a data-protection duty (P50), not an integrity rule.
units.anchor: is required by Section 5 of Lehigh’s Acceptable Use Policy to report the incident
units.frag_end: Office of Information Security at security@lehigh.edu
units.policy: Any member of the Lehigh community who learns of a potential breach of data protection or confidentiality, through Generative AI tools or otherwise, is required to report the incident to the Office of Information Security.

units.why: Faculty 'are expected to follow' the research-conduct policy, so AI in research defers to an existing research rule (P62).
units.anchor: University Policy on Ethical Conduct in Academic Research, Scholarship and Creative Activities
units.policy: Faculty are expected to follow the University Policy on Ethical Conduct in Academic Research, Scholarship and Creative Activities.

units.why: Students 'are expected to follow course-specific rules set by their instructors', so the rule is set per instructor (P04), not by the university.
units.anchor: follow course-specific rules set by their instructors
units.frag_end: as captured in the Student Code of Conduct
units.policy: Students are expected to follow course-specific rules set by their instructors.

units.why: The same sentence ties students to 'academic integrity rules set by the university'; this separate rule points to the Code of Conduct as the integrity process, so P36, while the instructor-rule half is P04.
units.anchor: academic integrity rules set by the university, as captured in the
units.frag_end: as captured in the Student Code of Conduct
units.policy: Students are expected to follow the academic integrity rules set by the university, as captured in the Student Code of Conduct.

units.why: Gives a security tip: 'do not use your Lehigh password' for outside apps; it protects accounts and credentials (P50).
units.anchor: do not use your Lehigh password
units.frag_end: do not use your Lehigh password

units.why: Says to 'always check the output for accuracy and bias' when using generative AI for professional work; verification duty, P31.
units.anchor: always check the output for accuracy and bias
units.frag_end: check the output for accuracy and bias

units.why: Tells users to 'appropriately cite any Generative AI tools that assisted in your work', a disclosure rule (P24); no tool/prompt detail is demanded so not P25.
units.anchor: appropriately cite any Generative AI tools that assisted in your work

units.why: Tells users to ask their chair or manager if unsure about using generative AI; this is the ask-first advice of P10.
units.anchor: Ask your chair, manager, or unit leadership if you have questions about using Generative AI
units.policy: Users ask their chair, manager, or unit leadership if they have questions about using Generative AI for academic, research, or administrative work.

units.why: Asks instructors to 'make AI "cheating" both less necessary and less appealing' while fostering authentic learning, a learning-rationale statement (P41); P35 assignment redesign fits less since no assignment change is named.
units.anchor: make AI "cheating" both less necessary and less appealing
units.policy: Users foster authentic learning, uphold academic integrity, and make AI cheating both less necessary and less appealing, while preparing students for responsible AI-enabled practice.

units.why: Says the 'safest way' to keep data from training models 'is to use an approved AI tool like Gemini'; prefers vetted tools, P50 (P17 not chosen since no course tool is mandated).
units.anchor: use an approved AI tool like Gemini and other Google AI tools
units.policy: The safest way to ensure submitted data is not shared or used to train models is to use an approved AI tool like Gemini and other Google AI tools available through the Lehigh Google Workspace account.

units.why: Recommends opting out of data sharing with free tools: 'we recommend you always opt out'; a privacy rule (P50).
units.anchor: we recommend you always opt out of sharing data when using such systems

units.why: Instructors 'are advised to give students clear guidance on the use of Generative AI tools'; this asks for stated AI expectations (P09).
units.anchor: give students clear guidance on the use of Generative AI tools for coursework
units.policy: Instructors are advised to give students clear guidance on the use of Generative AI tools for coursework and research.

units.why: Points instructors to integrity vignettes 'to highlight relevant cases and communicate expectations'. It is a teaching aid for communicating integrity norms; P09 requires a syllabus statement, so no type fits.
units.anchor: Academic Integrity Vignettes to highlight relevant cases and communicate expectations
units.policy: Instructors use Lehigh's Academic Integrity Vignettes to highlight relevant cases and communicate expectations.
units.uncovered_note: Instructors use university integrity case vignettes as a teaching tool to communicate expectations

units.why: Warns that marketed tools 'may not meet the university's security, privacy, and compliance standards', steering users toward vetted tools (P50).
units.anchor: may not meet the university’s security, privacy, and compliance standards
units.policy: Off-the-shelf AI tools being marketed may not meet the university's security, privacy, and compliance standards for handling anything besides public data.

units.why: Tells anyone contracting an AI vendor to 'complete this GenAI Software Registry', an institutional review of AI vendors (P65).
units.anchor: contract with a vendor who offers Generative AI-related services, complete this GenAI Software Registry

units.why: Individuals and departments are 'strongly encouraged' to work with ITS so tools meet acceptable use and security needs: vendor/tool review (P65).
units.anchor: collaborate with ITS to ensure that the tool under consideration meets Lehigh’s acceptable use guidelines
units.policy: Any individual or department seeking guidance on Generative AI is strongly encouraged to collaborate with ITS to ensure the tool under consideration meets Lehigh's acceptable use guidelines.

documents.title: Our Guiding Principles
documents.summary: Five guiding principles for AI at Lehigh, offered as 'shared guideposts' rather than policy. They stress mission, human agency, AI capacity-building, experimentation, and lawful, ethical use, and leave teaching decisions to faculty.
documents.stance_why: The page states 'These principles are not intended to function as policy statements or a mandate' and 'Faculty should decide how AI is used in their teaching', so it sets no default stance and defers to faculty and units.

units.why: Says 'These principles are not intended to function as policy statements or a mandate', defining the status of the framework (P56).
units.anchor: These principles are not intended to function as policy statements or a mandate.

units.why: Calls the principles 'a common starting point to support units, departments, and teams' in local conversations: AI decisions are local (P04).
units.anchor: a common starting point to support units, departments, and teams
units.policy: The principles are a common starting point to support units, departments, and teams as they continue local, discipline-appropriate conversations about productive and responsible AI use.

units.why: Says the principles 'should be treated as a living framework' refined over time, so the framework will be revisited (P54).
units.anchor: These principles should be treated as a living framework

units.why: Commits to 'favor AI tools, platforms, and practices that expand access, reduce barriers'; an access and equity commitment (P51).
units.anchor: favor AI tools, platforms, and practices that expand access, reduce barriers
units.policy: Lehigh will favor AI tools, platforms, and practices that expand access, reduce barriers, and support an inclusive environment for everyone.

units.why: Says informed decisions not to use AI 'are appropriate outcomes of thoughtful evaluation and are supported by the university', leaving non-use to local choice (P04).
units.anchor: are appropriate outcomes of thoughtful evaluation and are supported by the university
units.policy: Informed decisions not to adopt AI tools, on pedagogical, ethical, research integrity, or values grounds, are appropriate outcomes of thoughtful evaluation and are supported by the university.

units.why: States 'Faculty should decide how AI is used in their teaching, research, and service', the clearest delegation to instructors (P04).
units.anchor: Faculty should decide how AI is used in their teaching, research, and service.

units.why: Says 'AI will not replace meaningful human judgment, decisions, relationships, care, or mentorship', a principle about human centrality (P56).
units.anchor: AI will not replace meaningful human judgment, decisions, relationships, care, or mentorship.

units.why: Says 'AI may assist human work' but intellectual effort and ownership 'must remain with the person'. P32 (student stays the thinker) fits better than P29 since the focus is effort and ownership of thinking.
units.anchor: ownership that define genuine learning, discovery, and creative production must remain with the person
units.policy: AI may assist human work, but the intellectual effort, responsibility, and ownership that define genuine learning, discovery, and creative production must remain with the person.

units.why: Promises 'training and support so students, faculty, and staff understand how AI tools and platforms function', building AI skill as a competency (P44).
units.anchor: We will provide training and support so students, faculty, and staff understand how AI tools
units.policy: Lehigh will provide training and support so students, faculty, and staff understand how AI tools and platforms function and can apply them effectively in their work.

units.why: Says the community needs 'the ability to critically evaluate and validate their results', a verification expectation (P31).
units.anchor: the ability to critically evaluate and validate their results
units.policy: Students, faculty, and staff need the ability to critically evaluate and validate AI results.

units.why: Commits to dialogue about AI's 'societal, economic, and environmental impacts', naming wider harms (P53).
units.anchor: societal, economic, and environmental impacts
units.policy: Lehigh will continue to create opportunities for open and critical dialogue about AI's capabilities and limitations and its societal, economic, and environmental impacts.

units.why: Says 'encouraging exploration and experimentation with AI across the university'; a default of welcoming AI (P02).
units.anchor: encouraging exploration and experimentation with AI across the university

units.why: Commits to 'rigorously and continuously assessing the impact of AI tools' in education, an evidence commitment (P55).
units.anchor: rigorously and continuously assessing the impact of AI tools and platforms in educational contexts
units.policy: In the educational domain, Lehigh will prioritize AI uses that improve student learning and outcomes, rigorously and continuously assessing the impact of AI tools and platforms.

units.why: Requires 'all AI use complies with existing policies, codes of conduct, and applicable laws', an institution-wide framework principle (P56).
units.anchor: ensuring that all AI use complies with existing policies, codes of conduct, and applicable laws

units.why: Commits to 'refraining from entering sensitive or high-level data into unvetted or insecure AI tools', a data rule (P50).
units.anchor: refraining from entering sensitive or high-level data into unvetted or insecure AI tools and platforms

units.why: States 'every individual is responsible for the work they produce' whether or not AI helped, an ownership rule (P29).
units.anchor: every individual is responsible for the work they produce
units.policy: Whether assisted by AI tools or not, every individual is responsible for the work they produce and the ideas they claim as their own.

units.why: Says Lehigh will 'set standards for how AI tools and platforms are procured, vetted, used and monitored'; institutional vendor review (P65).
units.anchor: set standards for how AI tools and platforms are procured, vetted, used and monitored
units.policy: Lehigh will set standards for how AI tools and platforms are procured, vetted, used and monitored.

units.why: Commits to 'appropriate human responsibility and review for high-impact uses', a governance principle (P56).
units.anchor: ensuring appropriate human responsibility and review for high-impact uses
units.policy: Lehigh will ensure appropriate human responsibility and review for high-impact uses of AI.

units.why: A footnote defines which AI the principles cover: 'computer-based systems that can generate text, images, code'; a scope definition (P61).
units.anchor: computer-based systems that can generate text, images, code, and other outputs

documents.title: Teaching at Lehigh: Policies, Guidance, and Syllabus Statements
documents.summary: A broad Provost page of teaching policies and syllabus statements. Its AI section is two sentences: Lehigh has no uniform AI policy, instructors set their own and state them clearly in syllabi.
documents.stance_why: The page says 'Lehigh does not have a uniform policy about the allowable use of AI in courses' and that 'Instructors are encouraged to develop their own policies', so the stance is delegation to instructors.

units.why: States 'Lehigh does not have a uniform policy about the allowable use of AI in courses', a fact that sets the rule per instructor (P04).
units.anchor: Lehigh does not have a uniform policy about the allowable use of AI in courses.
units.frag_start: Lehigh does not have a uniform

units.why: 'Instructors are encouraged to develop their own policies' places the choice with each instructor (P04).
units.anchor: Instructors are encouraged to develop their own policies
units.frag_end: about these policies in their syllabi
units.policy: Instructors are encouraged to develop their own policies.

units.why: Asks instructors 'to be clear and transparent about these policies in their syllabi', a syllabus-statement expectation (P09).
units.anchor: to be clear and transparent about these policies in their syllabi
units.frag_end: about these policies in their syllabi
units.policy: Instructors are encouraged to be clear and transparent about their AI policies in their syllabi.

documents.title: Report and Recommendations from Lehigh's Generative AI Advisory Group
documents.summary: A May 2025 advisory-group report that surveys faculty and staff AI use and makes five recommendations: department-led integration, AI-readiness for students, administrative adoption, shared infrastructure and training, and regular policy review. It is advisory and supports both AI adoption and non-use.
documents.stance_why: The report is a set of recommendations, not a rule; it wants to 'support faculty when they lean into AI as well as when they lean away' and asks departments to set expectations, so it sets no stance itself and delegates.

units.why: Records that the group was set up 'to assess the opportunities, support needs, and policy gaps', stating the purpose and scope of the effort (P56).
units.anchor: to assess the opportunities, support needs, and policy gaps related to generative AI

units.why: Says 'it is incumbent upon us to prepare our students' to make wise AI choices, an AI-readiness rationale (P44).
units.anchor: it is incumbent upon us to prepare our students to do the same
units.frag_start: In light of this fact, it
units.frag_end: prepare our students to do the same
units.policy: Lehigh is obliged to prepare its students to make wise choices about whether and how to adopt generative AI.

units.why: Warns failure to prepare students 'will negatively impact' their 'future-readiness' and Lehigh's competitiveness; the career rationale (P44).
units.anchor: Failure to do so will negatively impact not only on our students’ future-readiness

units.why: Cites a faculty survey of the uses 'faculty have adopted and are encouraging in their students'; evidence on AI use (P55).
units.anchor: faculty survey provides a sense of the uses faculty have adopted and are encouraging

units.why: Reports the student uses 'recommended or required' by faculty (writing support 24%, tutoring 16%), evidence not a rule (P55).
units.anchor: the most common uses recommended or required include enhanced writing and research support (24%)

units.why: Reports faculty 'concerns about diminished critical thinking, problem-solving skills (63%)', the learning-erosion worry (P41).
units.anchor: concerns about diminished critical thinking, problem-solving skills (63%)

units.why: Notes 'Faculty also want clear guidelines on AI use in syllabi and assignments', reporting a demand for syllabus statements (P09).
units.anchor: Faculty also want clear guidelines on AI use in syllabi and assignments

units.why: Reports faculty 'seek discounted access to paid AI tools', an access and cost need (P51).
units.anchor: They seek discounted access to paid AI tools

units.why: Suggests an 'institutional response, such as a center or institute' for AI research and education, an institution-level structure (P56).
units.anchor: we would be wise to support an institutional response, such as a center or institute

units.why: Encourages 'additional guidance specifically tailored to the work of researchers', i.e. AI in research (P62).
units.anchor: we encourage the development of additional guidance
units.policy: The report encourages the development of additional guidance specifically tailored to the work of researchers at Lehigh.

units.why: Lists staff concerns: 'loss of human connection, data privacy and security', plus ethics and bias; P53 (harms) chosen over P50 as the list is mainly ethical concerns.
units.anchor: Major concerns include the loss of human connection, data privacy and security

units.why: Urges 'continuing to support faculty when they prefer to prioritize' skills unrelated to AI, leaving each faculty member to choose (P04).
units.anchor: continuing to support faculty when they prefer to prioritize helping our students develop
units.policy: The report names continuing to support faculty when they prefer to prioritize helping students develop knowledge and skills that have nothing to do with automation, efficiency, or technological augmentation of human intelligence.

units.why: Says 'we should promote and support broader adoption of AI tools where such tools make sense', encouraging adoption (P02).
units.anchor: promote and support broader adoption of AI tools where such tools make sense for us

units.why: The same sentence says to 'promote deeper awareness of the ethical questions, biases, and technological limitations'; a harms-awareness item (P53), separate from adoption.
units.anchor: promote deeper awareness of the ethical questions, biases, and technological limitations
units.policy: Lehigh should promote deeper awareness of the ethical questions, biases, and technological limitations that may lead some to the purposeful non-use of AI.

units.why: Asks that teaching and research about AI be framed with 'ethical considerations, literacy about AI-generated misinformation'; ethics and bias (P53).
units.anchor: teaching and researching about AI with ethical considerations, literacy about AI-generated misinformation
units.frag_end: humanity, at the front and center
units.policy: We should conceptualize teaching and researching about AI with ethical considerations, literacy about AI-generated misinformation, awareness of biases and environmental impact, and humanity at the front and center.

units.why: Recommends the Provost and Deans 'task department chairs to lead faculty discussions', putting AI decisions at department level (P04).
units.anchor: task department chairs to lead faculty discussions on integrating generative AI into curricula
units.policy: The Provost and Deans task department chairs to lead faculty discussions on integrating generative AI into curricula and student learning.

units.why: Suggests departments become an 'AI Innovator' department for 'faculty development opportunities', faculty support (P63).
units.anchor: Consider becoming an “AI Innovator” department for enhanced AI resources
units.policy: Departments consider becoming an AI Innovator department for enhanced AI resources and faculty development opportunities.

units.why: Asks departments to 'Designate an AI Ambassador' for leadership; institutional structure for AI (P56).
units.anchor: Designate an "AI Ambassador" for department-wide leadership
units.policy: Departments designate an AI Ambassador for department-wide leadership and coordination with centralized efforts.

units.why: Asks departments to 'Discuss AI-related minors or tracks within majors', a curriculum step on AI skills (P44).
units.anchor: Discuss AI-related minors or tracks within majors.

units.why: Asks departments to 'Ensure language in syllabi and assignments convey AI expectations, both for use and non-use', a syllabus-statement rule (P09).
units.anchor: Ensure language in syllabi and assignments convey AI expectations, both for use and non-use.

units.why: Asks departments to 'Develop clear AI usage guidelines for instructors and students', a department-level framework (P56).
units.anchor: Develop clear AI usage guidelines for instructors and students.

units.why: Asks departments to 'Identify courses where AI education is essential', teaching AI as a skill (P44).
units.anchor: Identify courses where AI education is essential.

units.why: Proposes a promise: 'All students will leave Lehigh AI-ready, fully prepared to use AI tools'; career-readiness goal (P44).
units.anchor: All students will leave Lehigh AI-ready, fully prepared to use AI tools
units.policy: The President and Provost make an AI-readiness promise: all students will leave Lehigh AI-ready, fully prepared to use AI tools effectively and ethically, having had meaningful engagement with generative AI in their coursework and professional development preparation.

units.why: Proposes ways to 'identify and label AI-Intensive courses in registration systems'; a course-labeling step that matches no existing type.
units.anchor: identify and label “AI-Intensive” courses in registration systems
units.policy: The Interdisciplinary AI Hub develops ways to identify and label AI-Intensive courses in registration systems.
units.uncovered_note: Labeling AI-Intensive courses in the registration system so students can find them

units.why: Asks for ways to 'assess the impact of AI adoption on student learning outcomes' with AB testing: evidence on learning (P55).
units.anchor: assess the impact of AI adoption on student learning outcomes
units.policy: The Office of the Vice Provost for Educational Innovation and Assessment develops scalable, low-effort ways faculty can assess the impact of AI adoption on student learning outcomes through targeted interventions with AB testing.

units.why: Proposes to 'Launch an AI micro-skills badge program for students', crediting AI skill (P44).
units.anchor: Launch an AI micro-skills badge program for students

units.why: Asks Career Services to continue 'guidance to students on effective use of AI' in the job search, a professional-skill item (P44).
units.anchor: Continue integrating guidance to students on eﬀective use of AI
units.policy: Career and Professional Development continues integrating guidance to students on effective use of AI in professional development and in the job search.

units.why: Asks LTS to 'Maintain access to, and promote, secure, free or low-cost AI tools' by name, i.e. university-provided tools (P17).
units.anchor: Maintain access to, and promote, secure, free or low-cost AI tools
units.policy: LTS maintains access to, and promotes, secure, free or low-cost AI tools like ChatGPT Sandbox, Gemini, and LibreChat Gateway.

units.why: Asks LTS to 'Expand and publicize vetted paid AI tools', provided sanctioned tools (P17).
units.anchor: Expand and publicize vetted paid AI tools for broader campus use
units.policy: LTS expands and publicizes vetted paid AI tools for broader campus use (Gemini Pro, Microsoft CoPilot).

units.why: Plans a student workshop on 'how to access and use vetted AI tools responsibly', teaching AI use as a skill (P44).
units.anchor: how to access and use vetted AI tools responsibly
units.policy: AI workshops for students cover how to access and use vetted AI tools responsibly and effectively.

units.why: Plans faculty workshops on 'adaptive teaching, curriculum development, learning assessment, tutoring, research support', faculty support (P63).
units.anchor: For faculty: adaptive teaching, curriculum development, learning assessment, tutoring, research support.

units.why: Asks LTS to 'oﬀer guidance on both AI-engaged and AI-resilient teaching and assignments'; assignment design around AI (P35).
units.anchor: guidance on both AI-engaged and AI-resilient teaching and assignments
units.policy: LTS continues to offer guidance on both AI-engaged and AI-resilient teaching and assignments.

units.why: Asks to 'An annual review of AI-related policies is recommended', a regular review (P54).
units.anchor: An annual review of AI-related policies is recommended

units.why: Asks LTS with the Provost's Office to 'draft an AI Policy Statement', an institution-wide framework (P56).
units.anchor: draft an AI Policy Statement, in line with recent guidance from Middle States
units.policy: LTS works with the Provost's Office to draft an AI Policy Statement, in line with recent guidance from Middle States.

units.why: Committees should 'review AI-related policies twice a year'; scheduled revisiting of policy (P54).
units.anchor: review AI-related policies twice a year
units.policy: The ACIS, ISSC, Data Governance Committee, and CGRC review AI-related policies twice a year to discuss if the policy is meeting university needs, and make updates and recommendations as needed.

units.why: Asks the Office of Research to 'develop a guiding statement for faculty on using AI in Research', research and scholarship (P62).
units.anchor: develop a guiding statement for faculty on using AI in Research

units.why: Asks Student Conduct to update the Code 'to explicitly name generative AI tools', tying AI misuse to the conduct process (P36).
units.anchor: updating the Student Code of Conduct to explicitly name generative AI tools
units.policy: The Office of Student Conduct continues work updating the Student Code of Conduct to explicitly name generative AI tools in relevant sections.

units.why: Asks offices to 'update all Academic Integrity websites, guidance pages, and communications' so advice is consistent; no type covers keeping integrity guidance consistent.
units.anchor: update all Academic Integrity websites, guidance pages, and communications
units.policy: The Office of Student Conduct, the Provost's Office and LTS update all Academic Integrity websites, guidance pages, and communications to ensure advice to faculty and students is clear and consistent.
units.uncovered_note: Keeping academic-integrity guidance for AI consistent across university websites and communications

notes: Coded by Coder B. Provost teaching page: only the AI paragraph was coded; the other teaching, accommodation and integrity sections are not AI-specific. Class I/II data text appears twice on the policies page and was coded once. In the advisory report, ligature characters in the saved text were kept in a few anchors/fragments so they match verbatim.
